homotopy.reason: Ordinary dominated-vertex folds of the deletion define a replayable simplicial retraction onto a certified sphere wedge. Every vertex of the link maps into an induced subcomplex with a universal vertex (a cone). Thus the link inclusion is nullhomotopic even without a dimension gap, and its cofiber splits into the deletion wedge, suspended link components and r-1 circles [Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 0].

Each vertex-link component has a graph-theoretically certified wedge-of-spheres homotopy type, and deletion s-collapses to a certified wedge of spheres of dimensions >=d>=2 (or a cone). Every link sphere dimension is <d, hence its component's attaching map is nullhomotopic by (d-1)-connectivity. The vertex-star homotopy cofiber splits into the deletion, suspensions of link components, and r-1 circles [Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 0].

Verified facet-greedy discrete Morse matching [Forman1998], plus exact rational top homology on a dimension-bounded collapse core. With one critical vertex and critical cells only in consecutive dimensions m,m+1 (m>=2), the maximal top Betti number forces zero cellular boundary. Hurewicz for a wedge of m-spheres makes the attaching maps nullhomotopic. With one critical 1-cell, the same zero boundary proves zero-degree attachments into the single circle [Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 4.2].

Verified facet-greedy discrete Morse matching [Forman1998], plus exact rational top homology on a dimension-bounded collapse core. With one critical vertex and critical cells only in consecutive dimensions m,m+1 (m>=2), the maximal top Betti number forces zero cellular boundary. Hurewicz for a wedge of m-spheres makes the attaching maps nullhomotopic. With one critical 1-cell, the same zero boundary proves zero-degree attachments into the single circle [Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 4.2].
